title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Medulin, Croatia 2027 Guide
metaDescription: Does Medulin have all-inclusive hotels? TUI Blue Medulin and Arena Hotel Holiday compared, with per-person prices vs half-board and apartments.
content:
## Does Medulin Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Yes, but the choice is small. Medulin is mostly a resort of mid-range hotels, apartments, mobile homes and campsites, so all-inclusive is the exception. Two hotels sell it, and they suit very different guests. Many other hotels in the area offer only bed-and-breakfast or half-board.

### TUI Blue Medulin

This is the only true all-inclusive hotel in Medulin, and every guest is on the all-inclusive plan. It is an adults-only hotel (16+) on the edge of the village, about 100 m from a sand-and-pebble beach. It has two restaurants and three bars. It also has a spa with a sauna, a gym and an evening entertainment programme. It scores around 4.4 out of 5 on Tripadvisor. Guests praise the service and the setting. The most common complaints are small rooms and drinks of modest quality.

### Arena Hotel Holiday

This 3-star family hotel near Bijeca beach, about 500 m away, has a pool and a Mini Club. In season it offers a Light All Inclusive plan. That plan covers full board, drinks with meals, an afternoon refreshment and selected sport activities. It is not a full all-inclusive: there is no all-day bar, and drinks outside meals are usually extra. Confirm the exact plan for your dates when booking, because Light All Inclusive is seasonal.

### Hotels Not to Assume

Several other Medulin hotels appear in all-inclusive search filters, including some upscale and spa properties. Most of these filters match any board type, so treat them with caution. Check the meal plan on the booking page before you pay.

## What Is Typically Included

At TUI Blue Medulin the plan covers:

- Breakfast, a late breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks
- Local and international drinks, including wine, beer and cocktails
- Weekly themed buffets, such as a gala dinner and a local-cuisine dinner
- A four-course à la carte dinner, which needs advance booking
- Gym and some wellness access, with certain treatments paid separately

Premium spirits and specialty drinks are extra. The Light All Inclusive at Arena Hotel Holiday is narrower: meals, mealtime drinks, an afternoon snack and sports.

## Price Per Person Per Night: Peak vs Shoulder Season

The figures below are rough ranges for two adults sharing a double room. Exact rates depend on the date, the room type and whether the booking is a package with flights.

- **All-inclusive (TUI Blue Medulin):** about €110–150 in July and August, and about €65–95 in May, June and September.
- **Light All Inclusive (Arena Hotel Holiday):** about €80–120 in peak and €50–70 in shoulder season.
- **Half-board in a 3-star hotel:** about €65–95 in peak and €45–60 in shoulder season.
- **Private apartment, self-catering:** about €30–55 per person in peak, assuming €90–160 per night for a 2–4 person unit, and about €20–30 in shoulder season.

The extra cost of all-inclusive over half-board is about €25–50 per person per night in peak. For that you get drinks and snacks, which are expensive at Croatian beach bars.

## Who Medulin All-Inclusive Suits

### Couples and short stays

TUI Blue Medulin fits couples on 3–7 night breaks who want to stop planning and just rest. Costs are fixed in advance, and the beach is 100 m away. Pula airport is about 10–15 km away, so transfers are short.

### Families with small children

TUI Blue Medulin is adults-only, so it is not an option for families with small children. The realistic family choice is Arena Hotel Holiday and its Light All Inclusive. It has a Mini Club and a pool, and it is close to a family-friendly beach. A family of four on a one-week stay should still compare it with an apartment. Children's meal portions at hotel buffets are rarely cheap, and apartment space matters at nap time.

### Who should self-cater

Anyone staying more than a week, travelling in a group of four or more, or planning to explore the area is better off in an apartment. Medulin's apartments are plentiful, and groceries are cheap. A day trip to Cape Kamenjak or Pula will mean skipping hotel meals anyway.

All-inclusive looks like the safe budget choice, but in Medulin it often is not. If you go out for lunch or spend the day at Kamenjak, you pay for meals you do not eat. Two or three skipped lunches wipe out most of the saving over half-board.

## Nearest Alternatives Outside Medulin

All-inclusive is thin on the ground near Medulin. Premantura, about 5 km south, has only small hotels that mainly sell bed-and-breakfast. Check the meal plan before assuming all-inclusive. Pula, about 10–12 km away, has larger hotels, but they mostly sell half-board or breakfast. The best choice for a full all-inclusive stay in the area is TUI Blue Medulin itself.

## Insider Tips

- Book all-inclusive for May–June or September. Rates drop by about a third, the sea is warm enough for swimming, and the hotel is far less busy.
- Ask about drinks policy. Premium spirits are usually excluded, so beer and wine drinkers get the most value.
- Half-board plus a free-choice beach bar tab often costs less than all-inclusive for light drinkers.
- The local bus to Pula stops near the hotel area but runs infrequently. Check the timetable before planning day trips.
- Peak-season apartments close to the beach go early. Book by January for August.

## Is All-Inclusive in Medulin Worth It?

It is worth it for adults wanting a low-effort break at a hotel with a strong review record. For families, long stays and travellers who want to explore, an apartment with an occasional restaurant meal gives better value and more flexibility. Medulin works best when you eat out, not when you stay inside a hotel buffet.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Medulin?
faq.answer: Yes. TUI Blue Medulin is fully all-inclusive and adults-only (16+), about 100 m from the beach. Arena Hotel Holiday offers a Light All Inclusive during the season.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost per person in Medulin?
faq.answer: Roughly €110–150 per person per night in peak season at TUI Blue Medulin, and about €65–95 in shoulder season. Light All Inclusive at Arena Hotel Holiday is cheaper, around €80–120 in peak. Rates vary by date, so check live prices.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive in Medulin good for families with small children?
faq.answer: TUI Blue Medulin is not, as it only takes guests aged 16 and over. Arena Hotel Holiday has a Mini Club and a pool and is the family-oriented option. Its all-inclusive is the lighter version, so check what is covered.

faq.question: Is half-board or all-inclusive cheaper in Medulin?
faq.answer: Half-board is cheaper, usually by €25–50 per person per night in peak season. All-inclusive pays off only if you eat lunch at the hotel and drink several times a day. Light drinkers and day-trippers save money with half-board.

faq.question: Is an apartment cheaper than all-inclusive in Medulin?
faq.answer: Yes, in most cases. A self-catering apartment costs roughly €30–55 per person per night in peak season, compared with €110–150 at the all-inclusive TUI Blue Medulin. The gap grows with larger groups.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive to Medulin?
faq.answer: The best option is in Medulin itself, at TUI Blue Medulin. Premantura, about 5 km away, and Pula, about 10–12 km away, have hotels, but most sell breakfast or half-board only. Check the meal plan before booking.

quickAnswer: Yes, Medulin has all-inclusive, but only a few hotels. TUI Blue Medulin is all-inclusive but adults-only (16+). Arena Hotel Holiday, the family option, offers a Light All Inclusive in season. Expect roughly €80–150 per person per night in peak and €50–95 in shoulder season. Apartments are usually cheaper.
